description:
1 or 2 people, the founders of Duo. Carlos Robles-Shanahan and Rafael Robles

Duo is a Chicago-based innovation studio/lab with the mission to create built environment innovations for the benefit of society. Duo's signature design methodology, Multicontextual Design, promotes norm/form-making which enables us to (re)shape dominant norms and set new precedents through our work.


The presentation will give a foundation of the importance and impact of real estate assets on the unequal distribution of wealth in the United States, and follow it with a presentation of two projects that will be among the first in Chicago to use equity crowdfunding to open investment opportunities for commercial and residential buildings to neighbors and non-accredited investors. speakers.name: Carlos Robles-Shanahan
speakers.bio: Carlos Robles Shanahan is the co-founder and director of Duo. An innovation studio that works to create built environment innovations for the benefit of society, Duo partners with organizations of all types through design, strategy, and innovation services, and by launching ethical real estate development and related ventures. Duo’s multicontextual design approach investigates and activates knowledge, wisdom, and beauty across a generative and evaluative process that explores Norm/Form-making. Their studio applies the lenses of economics, ecology, technology, culture, and ethics to enrich their practice and ensure that their innovations provide a societal benefit. Prior to Duo, Carlos worked as a strategy consultant for the Monitor Institute by Deloitte, as a researcher at the University of Michigan, and as a Chicago Public School teacher. His work spans the development and implementation of initiatives related to organizational strategy, education, immigration, economic development, and urbanization. Carlos earned a master’s in public policy from the University of Michigan, a bachelor of arts and science degree from Loyola University Chicago, and an associate’s degree from Harper College.

name: Block Packing: Reducing L1 Costs
description: Today, each Starknet block is associated with a fixed Layer 1 (L1) costs, meaning these costs increase linearly with the number of blocks. Applicative Recursion decouples blocks from L1 costs by spreading the cost over a batch of multiple blocks. This allows us to increase block frequency and also reduce operating costs. In this talk, you’ll learn about the necessary updates to Starknet and its proof system, SHARP, to make this possible, and how it moves us closer to decentralization

name: Repurposing of city owned buildings
Where crypto has product-market fit today
description:
Crypto has now been around over a decade: Bitcoin since 2012, and Ethereum since 2014. After 10 years it is appropriate for a company or project to evaluate the technologies they have built in terms of product-market fit with users. Crypto is no longer a new category with yet-undefined use cases and infinite potential promise. Though crypto may still be at the beginning of its story as an asset class with far further to grow, compared to established asset classes like real estate and gold, or even compared to the total market cap of Apple stock, it’s mature enough to make the claim some use cases have traction while others have been rejected. The factors taken into account when trying to value a project or company are usually product-market fit with users and revenue. For a mature company FDV is a fairly standard multiple of revenue. For a less mature company usage even if it isn’t driving revenue factors in. That’s why evaluating crypto so far for true PMF is essential to understanding the value of what we’ve built so far, and the potential routes toward crypto creating more value in the future.

In this talk, I explain with stats and stories where crypto has PMF today, separate from speculative use cases and financial games speculators play within a closed-loop onchain system. It’s fair to say closed-loop onchain financial games, which are most of DeFi, count as crypto product-market fit. However, these applications only solve problems for users that crypto itself created, so the amount of net user problems solved is 0. I’ll define PMF for this purpose as solving a problem and having traction with users in a way that exists outside of crypto. None of this is to say DeFi or even speculators do not serve a useful market function; they absolutely do. If we’re going to build an alternative financial system, it needs all the same financial tools as the traditional one, and more, that are desirable specifically to crypto users, that are enabled and unlocked only by the capabilities of blockchain. Speculators, too, are useful in terms of taking on risk on behalf of the rest of the market. But in order to have a conversation about PMF, we need to talk about users solving real problems with crypto, and projects that are earning revenue.

name: JAM
Restoring nature in everyday life
description: Nature is coming back, and in unexpected ways. Once-extinct peregrine falcons are also nesting in power stations, wolves are living in closed coal mines and beavers have found new habitats in cities such as Prague. For decades, we have protected national parks and endangered species. But in the meantime, we have lost much of the everyday nature that was part of our everyday life. Common birds, bees and butterflies have largely disappeared from European landscapes, as have flowering meadows, free-flowing rivers and wild wetlands. We cannot and will not go back to the past. But perhaps there is a lesson to be learned. Could an abundant and rich natural world become part of an urbanised society, a modern economy and a technological world? There has been much talk about rewildling of remote uplands, forests and coasts. Nevertheless, we can restore nature in everyday landscapes, in cities and in our neighbourhoods: as long as we put right policies in place and - perhaps most importantly - find good economic incentives.

name: Making Future Communities Real: 20th Century Efforts, 21st Century Projects & Guiding Principles
description:
The heart of a promising, grounded vision for the future of humanity centers around reconnecting deeply to self, to community, and to nature …if we are to move beyond the hyper disconnection, mass mindless consumerism, and meaningless of post-modern, anti-cultural economies... and in order to sail through the increasingly volatile waves of change brought by global warming and accelerating technologies.

But how do these visions for community become real?  
What can we learn from the principles and approaches underlying past and current efforts?
Where is the emerging edge?

We will quickly review the proto-experiments of the 20th century and their underlying philosophies: from the Goethenanum to Damanhur; from Black Mountain College to EPCOT; from Esalen Institute to Burning Man.

And show how these evolved into current experiments: US and Latin American projects, apocalyptic escapes, psychedelic retreats, and de-centralized communities.

We'll use all of these examples to surface and explore the meta-frameworks and long-term thinking that can help guide us into grounding and realizing a reconnected life-way for humanity through our projects.

name: Why Climate Fiction Matters
description: Climate fiction, or "cli-fi," is a genre of literature that explores the potential consequences of anthropogenic climate change on human societies and the environment. It has become an increasingly popular and relevant form of storytelling in recent decades due to the intensification of global warming and the growing public awareness of its implications. As the consequences of climate change become more apparent and pressing, climate fiction will likely continue to evolve in response to the shifting socio-political landscape. In a world grappling with the existential threat of climate change, the role of artistic narratives—particularly science fiction—becomes not just an aesthetic choice but a moral imperative. It's not a passive genre; it's a call to action. It motivates us to participate in shaping our future rather than being mere spectators. It's the narrative equivalent of "Bodhisattva Vow"—a commitment to work for the enlightenment and liberation of all sentient beings.

name: Crowdinvesting with GmbH-Token: Christoph Jentzch
Building A Decentralized Consumer Price Index (CPI): A Paradigm Shift in Economic Transparency
description:
The CPI methodology faces age-old criticisms: 
1) Substitution bias occurs when consumers switch to cheaper items during budget constraints. 
2) Lagged inclusion of new items results in outdated measurements. 
3) Quality changes aren't adequately considered. 

While efforts to address these persist, a more significant issue arises: 
4) Conflict of interest, as seen in Argentina, where governments manipulate CPI for policy objectives. Centralization and lack of transparency exacerbate this. Open networks offer a solution by allowing for transparent data access and verification.

I'll introduce D-FACTO as a framework for a decentralized CPI, exploring the potential of open networks, decentralized oracles, and transparent data collection. The talk will highlight the benefits of data and methodology transparency, utilizing decentralized networks to mitigate conflicts of interest. By sharing insights into D-FACTO's structure and incentives for decentralized oracles, data scrapers, and AI automated product classification, I aim to provide a roadmap for creating a decentralized CPI. This talk not only exposes the limitations of the current system but also outlines a revolutionary approach to a more transparent and accountable measure of inflation, fostering economic trust and informed decision-making.

name: Seeds of Change: Cultivating Regeneration in Urban Spaces
description:
Through a regenerative culture, we can revitalize and reinvent our societies, fostering harmony with nature. Inspired by its principles, we aim not just for sustainability but for rebuilding and renewing ecosystems and social structures. Unlike mere restoration, regeneration transforms our identity from rulers to stewards of the Earth, fostering co-evolution with all life.
Drawing on positive visions of a regenerative culture, we envision cities as catalysts for change, where communities thrive in symbiosis with their environment. 
To navigate this shift effectively, we must cultivate future skills—competencies translating knowledge into action. Each individual plays a vital role in supporting the more beautiful world our hearts know is possible.

name: Growing Community Ecosystems: Quadratic Funding, Project Incubation, and Web2 Empowerment
description:
Want to make an impact on the local level? My talk outlines methods for developing and sustaining vibrant local web3 communities to drive a Solarpunk future forward, focusing on local quadratic funding rounds, project incubation, and leveraging Web2 partnerships with already established partners like nonprofits. 

The goal is to create strong local economies within the web3 space, support grassroots projects, and bring together different technologies for mutual benefit. I'll use examples to show how these strategies can work in practice from my experience running a local node of the ReFi DAO in Colombia, offering takeaways for those looking to build or enhance web3 communities.

name: You have nothing to hide! Vol.2
description: We all have stuff to hide. Our thoughts, our actions, our connections. Sometimes it is to preserve our lifes, sometimes it is just the discomfort of revealing. We should be able to reveal our private matters on our own terms. For that we need privacy to be there from the get go - baked into the fabric of our cyberspace interactions. Privacy is not something to be added retrospectively. Let's look into how privacy can be preserved in online communication. What features are required for a tool/infra to be recognized as privacy preserving? How can zero-knowledge technology help? Let's also touch on the interesting projects in the space. My goal for this talk is to make you think about privacy every day!

name: “Optimistic” Outlook: Privacy in On-Chain AI Made Affordable
description: Our idea marries Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning (zkML), the hottest field in the ZK space, with Optimistic Machine Learning (opML), a promising alternative with longer finality. Our session will cover the technical details of how combining the two will unlock affordable privacy.

name: Usability vs Security in storing your crypto
description:
Securing your crypto assets was, is and will always be paramount, but it often comes at the expense of usability. This presentation aims to unravel the complex tapestry of self custody and why it really matters.

Join us as we compare and contrast different storage methods, including keeping your keys on your own computer, entrusting them to exchanges like Coinbase or Revolut, and the nuanced world of software and hardware wallets. We'll take an in-depth look at the pros and cons of each approach, providing clarity and guidance for beginners and seasoned investors alike.

Whether you're looking to secure your first token or optimise your current strategy, this talk will equip you with the knowledge you need to make informed decisions that best suit your needs".

name: Extending ETH with ICP
description:
The Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) is a blockchain based on threshold cryptography, state machine replication, and a novel consensus algorithm.

It was carefully designed to give smart contracts near native performance and scalability while maintaining the security of decentralized execution.

Another important design aspect of ICP is its seamless and secure integration with existing ecosystems like Bitcoin and Ethereum, but also traditional web services, leveraging threshold signatures and HTTPS outcalls.

In this workshop, you'll get an introduction to ICP with a focus on its Chain Fusion superpowers. Furthermore, you'll dive into a starter project that demonstrates how ICP smart contracts can be used to extend Ethereum and EVM smart contracts in powerful ways with applications to DeFi, NFTs, and governance.

This will give you the perfect basis to build powerful cross-chain applications with minimal effort and will set you up for success in competing for our bounty.

name: Bank3: efficient temporary shielding of assets
description: Bank3 is a generic method to enable cryptocurrency transfers whose beneficiary remains private until the assets are withdrawn. The fact that the recipient is eventually known means that there should be no legal issues. We will show how Bank3 works in practice (on Ethereum testnet) and will also describe a "dark" variant of Bank3 in which the receiver maintains privacy. Bank3 generalizes stealth addresses to the DAO and identity-based settings.

name: Build and secure your use of a dApp with hardware device
description: We will build a quick dApp and show how it's easy to integrate the possibility to use it with a hardware device and secure our use of it.

name: Making Product Development Rock with Awesome Developer Experience (DX)
description:
In Ethereum's fast-evolving tech platform, prioritizing positive Developer Experience (DX) is crucial. This should be integrated into every phase of the product cycle, making sure that DX and Developer Relations (DevRel) are at the core of the development process. This strategic approach drives innovation, increases engagement, and empowers the community.

Join us to refine and perfect the Ethereum platform. Together, let's build an inclusive, streamlined, and open web3 ecosystem where a stellar developer experience is integral to our success.

name: Enhancing vulnerability detectors with LLM
description: The rapid growth of AI is already making waves in our industry. How can we leverage this technology for static analysis to create more precise vulnerability detectors for our smart contracts? This talk will dive into the development process and explore the bright future that lies ahead.

name: Layer 2 Interoperability with BaaS (Bridge as a Service)
description:
The modular blockchain trend will continue to break down the infrastructure of the Ethereum ecosystem into multiple layers. The market was decimated by Covid, but in the meantime the blockchain infrastructure has been rapidly developing. This is a sign that the era of DApps is upon us once again.
However, the development of infrastructure layers has led to a flurry of projects, and DApps still suffer from fragmented interoperability. The Bridge as a Service (BaaS) is the solution to this problem. My session will introduce the trend of BaaS in the Layer 3 era.

name: Solidity VS Code extensions for development & security
description: Visual Studio Code extensions improve the smart contract development process in productivity, but it can also be an early stage security tool. Every Solidity extension has different features; from syntax highlighting, code lens, or graphs to sophisticated static analysis and vulnerability detections. Let’s compare the strengths and weaknesses of the most popular extensions and find the ultimate combo for code security.

name: A new paradigm in privacy: The Fundamentals of Homomorphic Encryption
description: Privacy and data security are becoming ever more important, not only in blockchain, but throughout the digital landscape. Moreover, before blockchain can move to a modular future, the industry needs to find ways to keep data secure and private across different domains. Homomorphic encryption (HE), or specifically Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), is emerging as an answer, since it enables computing over encrypted data. Effectively, it has the potential to create a new paradigm of interoperability among entities by enabling data to be used across domains while mitigating (some) concerns related to privacy and data leaks. But as with all new technologies, HE still faces certain challenges that must be addressed before it can be widely implemented. This presentation will delve into the fundamentals and provide necessary context covering the basics of FHE schemes as well as the challenges to make FHE feasible in current systems. It will also compare different privacy solutions, explore practical use cases and give an overview of projects shaping the FHE space.

name: Beyond CREATE2: Smart Contract Multi-chain Deployments with CREATEX, YAC3F, and Foundry
description: This journey unfolds against the backdrop of 2023, marked by collaborative efforts to facilitate CREATE3 same address deployment across multiple chains. The culmination in late 2023 saw the successful deployment of the required infrastructure. The talk unveils indispensable tools and outlines a decision-making process, empowering developers with insights on when and how to leverage these tools effectively.

name: Daydream Believers - Solarpunk Island
description:
In this session, we explore our Solarpunk Island challenge, captivating 7-15 year-olds by intertwining nature, technology, and social advancement within Daydream Believers' inventive educational frameworks, all through the inspiring prism of Solarpunk ideals.

We will spotlight this creative initiative, a freely accessible resource on the Daydream Believers website, designed to foster environmental stewardship and innovative problem-solving. Participants are encouraged to thoughtfully engage in shaping a greener world, using collective, hands-on activities set within an imaginative, fictional landscape.

With participation from 48 schools, we aim to share inspiring tales from this impactful learning journey, showcasing how it equips young minds to tackle tomorrow's challenges with inventiveness, compassion, and a keen environmental conscience. 

Come join us on the island and share your thoughts on our call to action - What if we get it right?

name: The Social Credit System in the People's Republic of China. Origins, Plans, and the State of Affairs.
description:
The Chinese Social Credit System plans exist much longer than is publicly known. Being a means of power of an authoritarian state it nevertheless (or precisely for this reason) has rational motifs and structures that are comparable to western role models.
From a visit to the country evidence was gathered showing who actually is subject to these means and how far the goals have been achieved until now.

name: Oracles Reimagined: How L2 State Diffs Change Game
description: I'll present a design, limitations and innovation of the State Diffs Oracle, which allows for updating data feed each 1-sec on-chain and paying only for one update in each L2 block. It's a frontier of innovation in the on-chain oracle design.

description:
