name: EthStorage - Building a Modular Storage Layer for Ethereum on EIP-4844
description: EIP-4844 is the much anticipated native Ethereum data availability (DA) solution in the upcoming Ethereum Cancun upgrade.  However, to limit the storage requirement of the validators, EIP-4844 will discard the DA data (namely binary large objects, BLOBs) older than 18 days. In this talk, we introduce EthStorage, an Ethereum L2 solution to offer long-term available solution for EIP-4844 BLOBs with on-chain proof of storage verification.  By indexing the BLOBs on-chain and storing BLOBs off-chain, EthStorage can scale to hundreds of Terabytes or even Petabytes at 1/100x to 1/1000x of Ethereum storage cost. We will demonstrate the EthStorage testnet that is integrated with EIP-4844 on the Ethereum testnet, and showcase prototypes for new Ethereum applications like vitalik's blog, decentralized Dropbox, dynamic NFTs, etc.

name: PeerDAS, Ethereum danksharding v0
description: Ethereum scalability roadmap is focused on increasing its data throughput without sacrificing on decentralization. The currently agreed path to achieve so is Danksharding. Ethereum core devs are implementing today its first iteration: PeerDAS. PeerDAS re-uses battle-tested p2p components already in production in Ethereum to bring additional DA scale beyond that of 4844 while keeping the minimum amount of work of honest nodes.

name: Accelerate OP Fault Proof via EIP-4844-Powered Multi-Section Dispute Game
description: In this talk, we present an approach to significantly expedite the fault-proof dispute by implementing a multi-section search approach. In contrast to the current bi-section game, which demands log2(N) moves to identify the final disputable step, the K-section game (where K > 2) diminishes the moves to logK(N). However, in the K-section game, each player (defender/attacker) must publish a K-1 VM state hashes on-chain for each move. The introduction of EIP-4844 facilitates a substantial reduction in this cost through the utilization of EIP-4844 Binary Large Object (BLOB), capable of accommodating K=4096 VM hashes per BLOB. Consequently, for an N=2^48 game, the game can be condensed to 4 moves from the original 48 moves. This will significantly decrease the time elapsed for a fault-proof dispute game, from 2-3 days to a couple of hours.

name: Mass surveillance, digital freedom and cyber security
description:
This panel brings together leading scholars and practitioners to explore the intricate balance between security measures and the preservation of individual freedoms in the digital age.

Professor Martin Warnke from the Institute for Culture and Aesthetics of Digital Media (ICAM) will discuss the cultural implications of mass surveillance and its impact on aesthetics and the perception of privacy.

Pierre Sel from EastisRed will delve into the socio-political ramifications of surveillance practices within China and the EU. His analysis will focus on the evolving regulatory landscape, social credit, and the resistance movements that advocate for digital freedoms against the backdrop of increasing state surveillance.

Giulio Corsi from the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (LCFI) will examine the intersection of artificial intelligence and surveillance, offering insights into how AI technologies can both enhance and threaten cyber security. Corsi's work emphasizes the ethical considerations and potential biases inherent in AI-driven surveillance systems.

Dr. Hyun-Joo Lim will contribute a critical analysis of cyber security frameworks, emphasizing the need for robust protection mechanisms that do not infringe on civil liberties. Dr. Lim's expertise in international cyber policy will shed light on the global challenges and cooperative efforts required to safeguard digital freedoms while maintaining security.

Together, these experts will provide a comprehensive overview of the contemporary issues at the nexus of mass surveillance, digital freedom, and cyber security. The panel will engage with the audience in a dynamic discussion, aiming to forge a path forward that respects individual rights while addressing the imperatives of national and global security.

name: Green and blue infrastructure in cities in the light of economics and residents' preferences
description:
The number of people living in cities has increased rapidly in the last decades due to a rapid
population growth and, most importantly, increasing rates of urbanisation. The ongoing climate
change brings along phenomena that may have an impact primarily on city inhabitants in the future,
for example through water deficiency, (flash) floods, heat waves or drought. It is therefore necessary
that cities react to these new conditions and use adaptive measures to help their inhabitants to
adapt to climate change. We know how to do it, and we're excited to get started! Although Czech
cities are considered relatively green in international comparison, we cannot rely on current
measures. It is necessary to look for other places for greening such as green roofs and facades or blue
infrastructure elements, which are lacking in Czech cities.
The implementation of these measures is associated with a number of barriers (lack of funding and
incentives, priorities directed to other public service areas, conflicts of interest, etc.). Awareness of
both decision-makers and the general public plays an important role in this. The awareness and
therefore the acceptance of the measures can be increased through appropriate communication. The
results of economic assessment in the form of economic arguments play an important role in how to
present green and blue infrastructure in an easily understandable form.
To achieve these objectives, we can combine a number of methods, such as preference survey, cost-
benefit analysis, ecosystem services assessment, etc. The application of these methods in relation to
innovative examples of blue-green infrastructure elements and provided benefits will be the main
focus of the presentation.

name: Enter the Portal Network
description: The Portal Network is a new approach to an old problem. How can we provide lightweight access to the Ethereum protocol? By spreading the responsibilities of a full node out across a DHT, the Portal Network attempts to solve this problem. We'll discuss the current state of the Portal Network. What data is available? What data will be available? How is this data validated? And how you can access this data by running your own Portal Network Node.

name: Challenges of creating a sustainable and humane future for North Korea: core ideologies and their paradoxes
description:
This presentation aims to outline the core ideologies and major policies of North Korea that have been the building blocks of the regime’s political, economic, and ultimately human rights approaches in the name of realising a utopian vision of national security and independence. I seek to use this presentation as a point of discussion for a sustainable and humane future for North Korea. 
	Since Kim Jong Un’s reign in 2011, he has introduced some changes in the political economy, through the re- emphasis on economic development to improve people’s livelihoods. This is reflected in the shift in 2013 from the military- first Songun policy to the Byungjin policy, which entails the parallel development of both military and economic sectors. Nonetheless, there have been no profound or substantive changes in North Korean politics, and the vulnerability of the regime, which was established on the hereditary inheritance of power and its dictatorial rule depends heavily on the military for its own survival. Hence, the principle of Songun remains a dominant doctrine in policy making and the regime continues to rely on the revised historical narratives of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, the new blend of “Kimilsungism- Kimjongilism”, founded on the official autarkic state ideology, Juche (meaning ‘self-reliance’), in protecting independence and socialism. Paradoxical to self-reliance as a central pillar of its official ideology, the regime has heavily relied on international aid for food and to support economy. Together with this, the official version of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea's (DPRK) ‘our style human rights’ strongly represents collective rights and ideology, comprising four principal tenets: ‘(i) the right to national survival, (ii) dictatorship as the protection of human rights, (iii) granted by the fatherly leader, (iv) the use of duty-based language of human rights.’ Under these ideologies and government policies, the development of nuclear weapons has accelerated, whilst raising serious concerns about human rights, food security and economic sustainability of the country. 	
        I propose a sustainable and humane future for North Korea is achievable through bottom-up movements within the DPRK, in conjunction with collective pressures from international communities and nation-states.

name: Tools for the socio-economic renaissance
description:
The current economic network and organizing paradigm restricts autonomy and limits freedom. Communities have two options: to give up autonomy for the sake of interoperability - use infrastructure, protocols, and currencies operated and controlled by someone else, and thereby participate in wider economic networks - or to give up interoperability for the sake of autonomy - opt out of the shared infrastructure and produce everything themselves. Anoma aims to offer a third way - one which preserves both autonomy and interoperability. 

In this talk, we'll introduce Anoma as Ethereum's universal intent machine, then describe Anoma's affordances and how they provide developers and communities with tools to build socio-economic applications of the future by unbundling protocols (applications) from operators (Silicon Valley gatekeepers and wall st financiers). The heart of the talk will review a handful of Anoma's novel applications, including;

1. Public Signal - double/sided version of Kickstarter implemented with intents.  Possible to implement Alex Tabarrok's dominant assurance contracts. 
2. Multichat - a distributed and encrypted chat network without any specially designated server operators.
3. Promise Graph - a language and structured accounting logic for making and managing promises in and across distributed organizations. 
4. Scale-free money - a hypothetical monetary system design which allows anyone to create arbitrary denominations of money at any time for any purpose (inclusive of Multilateral Trade-Credit Set-off)
5. Time Banks - facilitate the trade of time for skills without needing “money” (in the traditional sense) as a medium of exchange.
6. Modular Logistics - unifies transport logistics providers under a common interface. Instead of contracting w/ individual providers, users contract w/ insurance providers, and buy a contract to transport them from a to b.

name: "Artistic Speculations and Ecofeminist Futures"
description: This talk offers a dive into the intersections of ecofeminism, sustainable technologies, and speculative futures through the lens of my artworks. The session will explore how these works reimagine the future and challenge current ecological and technological paradigms, envisioning a world where art, science, and activism meld to foster sustainable living and feminist ecologies.

name: Will your Oracle hug you or rug you?
description:
Hopefully by now, you all know [L2BEAT](https://l2beat.com/). The metrics shown there give a complex overview of what to look for in a Layer 2 solution. As we are scaling Ethereum to the next level (and hopefully **to the moon**, we have more and more new use cases for data to be brought from the physical world to the chain(s). 

That is why, we need the same level of due diligence and transparency for **oracle technologies**.

Whether it's price data or election results or the number of rabbits jumping around in [Ōkunoshima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Ckunoshima), it is extremely important to always have full **verifiability** and **availability** of the required information. That's the only way to NOT get rugged and be another story on [rekt](https://rekt.news/).

This talk will aim to provide a foundation in Oracles, empowering the developers of now and the future to make educated decisions on one of the most important pieces of third party infrastructure they will ever integrate. 

Can your Oracle hug you, or rug you? There’s only one way to find out…

name: MetaMask Snaps: Fostering Authentic and Extensible Wallet Innovation
description: we explore the transformative impact of Snaps permissionless innovation in the Wallet ecosystem. These community-driven events emphasize genuine, transparent interactions and have been instrumental in advancing the development of MetaMask Snaps, enhancing wallet functionality. We discuss how these gatherings have not only spurred interest and contributions within the MetaMask extension ecosystem but also attracted a diverse range of new contributors, enriching the Web3 developer community. Join us to discover how authentic relationships and collaborative innovation are reshaping wallet technology in Web3.

name: Introducing the Verifier Alliance (VerA)
description:
VERA aims to provide unified and open access to EVM smart contract source code. The initial outcome of the collective is a public SQL schema and a publicly accessible DB. The talk will be a showcasing for the VERA project.

Outline:
1. A brief introduction to the Sourcify project, our goals, what we are focusing on + what we're not, and our short roadmap.
2. The story of how VERA came to be and what problem we are solving
3. Technical outline of the database schema and its design rationale
4. Proposing the roadmap and other solutions that can be built on top of VERA

As the first talk on VERA in an ETH conference, it will serve two main goals:
1. Social: Spotlighting VERA within the Ethereum community. Reaching out to people and projects that can contribute or benefit from VERA
2. Technical: Showcasing the technical aspects and soliciting feedback on the current and proposed framework.

name: Where Opportunity Meets Power: Harnessing Gitpaid to Fuel Open Source Projects
description: Open source projects are vital to technological innovation but frequently face financial instability. Gitpaid addresses this crucial issue by harnessing GitHub's extensive network, enabling direct funding support from both individual users and institutions. In this talk, I'll discuss the challenges that open source developers encounter, such as inconsistent funding and limited project visibility, and demonstrate how Gitpaid offers practical solutions. Through real-world examples, we'll see how Gitpaid not only fosters financial empowerment but also strengthens the entire open-source ecosystem, ensuring that vital projects receive the support they deserve.

name: Two Minds, One Move: A Collaborative Chess Engine
description:
Instead of single player making decision we can have 2 or more people in one team (black or white team). 
**We don't do voting**, instead each player goes into a mini-game with their teammates showcasing their moves and counter moves. Once consensus is reached the move is made against the team(black or white).  

**example scenario** : suppose white team wants to make a move e4 but your teammate suggest h4 move. They both can play against each other countering each other moves. Once they reach consensus that move is played on the main game. the process repeats similarly for black team too. 

What's so different about this game
- people have done multiplayer chess in past too but it was always voting mechanism.
- In this game players have to literally defend their move against their teammate and thus the best move is always played against the team. 

repo : https://github.com/hackertron/Chess-machine

name: Security at the sequencer level
description: The Ethereum consensus protocol defines how transactions are included in blocks. It is accepted as fully decentralized and censorship-resistant, which means that it cannot provide any additional security guarantees to projects built on the Ethereum blockchain. Rollups have been broadly accepted as a promising scaling solution for Ethereum. A common architectural element of every rollup is the sequencer. The sequencer is responsible for collecting transactions from users and includes them in blocks. The ability to alter the rollup sequencing protocol presents a great opportunity to also alter the transaction inclusion rules and enhance them with additional features. This is amplified by the fact that most of the rollup sequencers that are currently used are centrally operated. In this paper, we describe the sequencing protocol of the Zircuit blockchain which includes additional scrutiny from the security perspective for transactions submitted to the sequencer. The protocol does not impose additional centralization that would not be already present in the existing sequencers. It still offers a high degree of censorship resistance, and allows for trustless rederivation of the rollup state. We present the protocol and consider practical aspects and the feasibility of implementing it using the OP stack and the mainstream Ethereum client Geth. The protocol is generic, meaning that it can be used for transaction filtering purposes other than those focused on security.

name: Login to Linux using Ethereum Name Service
description: N/A

name: Artificial intelligence, disinformation and the future of democracy
description: This talk discusses how cutting-edge AI technologies can disrupt democratic processes by amplifying false information, swaying public opinion, enabling mass surveillance and eroding trust in institutions. Yet, within this challenge lies opportunity—AI also offers powerful tools for identifying and neutralising false information at scale. This talk navigates through these contrasting roles of AI, highlighting both the perils and promises as we consider innovative strategies to reinforce democratic resilience against the rising tide of disinformation.

name: Making crypto space safer for the next billion users one community at a time
description:
Various ecosystems including Ethereum aim to onboard the next billion users to crypto, but all the scams, rug pulls, wash trading, hacks etc. making the space unsafe for newcomers.
Communities of all kinds, from project-centric to good cause driven, are the entry point for newbies.
We need to make it possible for all players to understand what’s going on in various communities, while support their members and joint activities.
And for this we require an authentication system for communities!

name: Building a developer ecosystem
description: Building a developer ecosystem is hard. Encode has helped build many over the years, helping with events, incubation and narrative building. We'll share our insights and guide on how to do it right! In this light, we'll also explore how you as an ambitious developer can benefit the most as an ecosystem grows from opportunities such as funding, founding startups, getting jobs and more.

name: ZK Proof Generation Infrastructure: Overhyped or Underutilized?
description: In the rapidly evolving ZK space, new concepts like zk marketplaces and zk proving services are emerging, yet the major zkL2s remain largely centralized in terms of proof generation. This scenario raises several critical questions: Is the centralization of proof generation in zkL2s a significant issue? If these platforms do not move towards decentralization, what other applications could drive the demand for zero-knowledge proof infrastructure?

name: Decentralize Your dApp’s Secret Off Chain Backend w/EigenLayer
description:
Many popular Web3 apps today rely on some amount of off chain backend services that are hosted in a centralized public cloud. Projects often start with some amount of centralization and include a "Roadmap for Decentralization", because the Ethereum community values and rewards further decentralization.

EigenLayer is a platform for shared security for Web3 services built on Ethereum that enables further decentrlization. This talk will include architecture guidance and examples of migrating a popular centralized Web3 backend service to EigenLayer.

name: Solving Vitalik's trilemma with zk-driven DA and Storage
description: zkSNARKs provide proofs of DA and storage as zk oracle, unlocking infinite recursion for rollups. Here ZeroPool provides a walkthrough of the components of our Sharded Storage and discusses the bottlenecks and tradeoffs on the way to building an infinite scalable L1-level soundness blockchain solution.

name: Eco Futurum
description: Eco Futurum - Gunilla Samberg

name: Enhancing AA with on-chain hierarchies: A New Approach
description:
The Palmera Module revolutionizes the creation and management of on-chain hierarchical structures, providing a robust solution for organizations, DAOs, and individuals managing multiple Safes. This innovative module allows users to establish customizable, flexible hierarchies that enhance decision-making processes and organizational governance. By enabling the construction of hierarchical Safes, it democratizes access and control, allowing upper Safes to have configurable rights over subordinate Safes, thereby streamlining governance and operational efficiency.

On-chain hierarchical structures are crucial for delineating clear roles, responsibilities, and authority levels within organizations. This not only facilitates effective management and accountability but also optimizes decision flows and operational directives across various organizational levels. The Palmera Module’s design emphasizes ease of use and functionality, allowing users to quickly set up and manage these structures with minimal hassle.

Key features of the Palmera Module include the ability to tailor each Safe with specific configurations and permissions, thus enabling organizations to adapt their governance models to meet their unique needs. For example, a Root Safe could delegate financial responsibilities to a Marketing Safe, allowing it to operate autonomously within predetermined limits, enhancing both security and operational autonomy.

Moreover, the module integrates seamlessly with externally owned accounts (EOAs) and other smart contracts, expanding the flexibility and potential configurations within the hierarchical structures. The Palmera Module not only simplifies the creation of such structures but also enhances their effectiveness, making it an indispensable tool for any entity looking to leverage blockchain technology for sophisticated, scalable governance solutions.

name: Reversing the innovation flow: having rollups lead the innovation in the Ethereum ecosystem
description: Ethereum has embraced a rollup-centric roadmap. Rollups are becoming increasingly mature. With efforts such as Rollup Improvement Proposals (RIPs), an inversion of the innovation flow is occurring. Formerly, upgrades would reach Ethereum L1 first, and rollups would adapt. Now, Rollups have specific needs, and push for upgrades that solve problems for them. This creates two externalities, one positive and one negative, respectively that protocol upgrades are more easily testable with more users and developers but that it creates potent EVM fragmentation risks.

name: Digital Slavery: From Chinese Social Credit System to American Mass Surveillance
description:
Main Questions to Address:
- Government Surveillance and Authority: With the increasing prevalence of mass surveillance
and data collection, what are the expanded powers and capabilities of governments? How do
these advancements affect the balance of privacy and security?
- Future Societal Transformations: What are the long-term impacts of technological and
militaristic political trends on society? How will we interact with the government in the future?
Will there be any?
- Perception and Reality of the Digital Landscape: How does our perception of the digital world
compare to our real-life interactions? Is the digital realm an extension of our physical world, or
does it constitute a distinct universe with its own rules and realities?

name: Envisioning Eco-Futures: Empowering Nature through Sovereignty and Innovation
description: "Envisioning Eco-Futures" explores the transformative potential of recognising and empowering nature as sovereign. We'll delve into how treating Real World Assets (RWA) as Real World Animals and achieving financial independence for ecological efforts and stewardship can shift their valuation from optional to essential. By integrating eco-data into the digital economy, we create indispensable assets that respect the complexity of interspecies co-existence and champion biodiversity. How innovative tools, such as Sovereign Nature Initiative’s  DEEP protocol and REAL portal, are pivotal in promoting ecological resilience and restoring biodiversity. Join us to explore actionable insights and the profound impact of cutting-edge technology in ecological conservation and community empowerment, steering us toward a truly interconnected and nature-positive future.

name: Powering up intents in DeFi
description:
This presentation will describe the use of intents in building a DeFi aggregation layer that will be easily accessible by any user or application. Combined with the automation tooling we have built, Mimic users will send thousands of intents automatically, based on predefined parameters.
The infrastructure we are building will be a gateway for any developer to interact with DeFi via a single API call.

name: Leveling Up the TEE Attestation Game On-Chain
description:
Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) technology is a cheap and fast solution to enhance blockchain applications like Co-Provers, Oracles, and MPC. To establish trust, a TEE must prove its identity on-chain through Remote Attestation, a cryptographic handshake that ensures its authenticity, integrity, and security. Every TEE can produce an attestation document endorsed by its maker, showcasing its secure enclave status, legitimate code execution, and untampered internals. But here’s the kicker: verifying the attestation document calls for the use of cryptographic primitives not natively supported by the EVM, such as the P-256 and P-384 curves, incurring costs of tens of millions in gas fees, and in some cases even exceeding the block gas limit.

However, there’s room for improvement: ZK extends our techniques for performing attestation verification and allows us to tap into off-chain resources to handle parts of the computation. Rather than performing on-chain verification of let’s say a P-256 signature, we craft a validity proof to confirm the correctness of the signature and verify this proof instead. To kick it up a notch, we leverage ZK aggregation and combine multiple validity proofs into a singular proof, significantly enhancing its efficiency and reducing costs along the way. The overall approach drives attestation verification costs down to around 300k gas, making it feasible on-chain.

name: Decentralized Outcome Funding for Investigative Reporting
description:
The broad idea behind Impact Certificates is that purchasing impact should be similar to how one buys a t-shirt. They overcome the issue of double selling of impact (create change once and then market to as many funders as possible) and giving donations based on brand rather than outcomes.

Incubated at Protocol Labs, Hypercerts are a web3 standard for impact certificates. This talk will go into a demo built by VoiceDeck in collaboration with the Ethereum Foundation to help traditional media newsrooms port their private database of impact as Hypercerts on Optimism.

Some of the topics we touch on;

- current problem in grant funding space around double selling of impact & reputation based donating
- integration with Hypercerts (web3 impact certs)
- quantification of impact via Benefit Cost Ratios
- North star: getting the Panama Papers onchain!
- Testnet demo with media outlets from India at app.voicedeck.org

name: Is Design the final frontier to mass adoption?
description:
In this Talk, I will delve into the topic of Design in the ecosystem, exploring how we can use it most effectively to reach a broad range of users. 
We'll cover best practices for web2 and innovative ideas and perspectives on where we are and where we want to be. 
As an ecosystem, our ultimate goal is to change the perception of value, identity, self-sovereign, and human coordination. We must take a fresh problem-solving approach using core design approaches and techniques to achieve this. 
I will discuss how Design can play a crucial role in shaping the next set of web3 products and how we can use it to drive sustainable growth and onboard the next billion users. 
The target audience is individuals who build or create new products and experiences on web3. My goal is to help them shift their perspective on improving the experience and developing a more user-centric web3 ecosystem.

name: Building an open commerce protocol as public infrastructure
description: The commerce protocol we introduce will be locked open at all levels with the aim of building for the common good. To do this, we will present an L2-like construction tailored for managing merchant and customer data. We will compare this to other protocol and infrastructure projects such as the ONDC, OpenBazzar and BTCPay Server. We will also explore how to preserve privacy while generating proofs of purchase and how these proofs could be used to build reputation and attribution systems. The result will be a system that when coupled with crypto as currency allows customers and merchants to regain sovereignty over their data and commercial interactions online and IRL.

name: Building DeFi Yield Curves & Unlocking New Real-World Use-Cases
description:
While DeFi has thrived in trading and farming, the absence of a strong foundation akin to traditional finance hinders its potential. The TradFi world would collapse if US Treasury markets disappeared tomorrow, yet that is where DeFi finds itself today. Scalable Fixed-Income markets offer opportunities to develop Forward Markets, thereby enhancing Options and Derivatives, creating Structured Products and unlocking a whole new world of real-life opportunities: present & future payments, cheap remittances to onboard new users, Real-World Asset tokenization & second order use-cases, Mortgages as well as healthy borrowing & lending solutions for the non-crypto native masses.
Recognizing this gap, Term Structure is on a mission to contribute to the development of yield curves within DeFi. As a speaker we are eager to leverage the platform to raise awareness and foster collaboration within the community, propelling DeFi forward.

name: Is DeFi Inclusive? Reimagining DeFi Towards Financial Empowerment
description:
The foundation of DeFi rests on the idea of fostering an inclusive financial environment. However, in reality, its success  hinges on TVL and related parameters, primarily sourced from whales, market makers and all sorts of degens. Consequently, DeFi products are tailored to this specific audience, neglecting those who could genuinely benefit from them. The complexity of products and interfaces, coupled with opaque setups, alienates many potential users who often cannot even percieve the relevant use cases. 

This presentation will delve into the existings hurdles and how to overcome them, for shifting  this focus and making DeFi more accessible to a wider audience, thereby enhancing its impact beyond just impact-driven projects,  providing financial self-sovereignty to those facing centralized interference and ultimately improving DeFi's public perception.

name: Empowering Communities and DAOs: How to Activate the “Unactivated”
description:
Anjali Young is the Co-Founder of Collab.Land. Anjali has been active in online communities since 1993 as both a member and in leadership positions. She will use her time at ETHPrague to discuss the issues of community members and how community leaders can bolster engagement for a more vibrant community. 

Her role at Collab.Land focuses on onboarding all types of tokenized projects and partners onto the platform, ensuring Collab.Land’s “community of communities” is a safe and welcoming space, and educating others about web3 ethos and values. Anjali has also worked as a lawyer, adjunct professor, and early tech startup employee. In addition to her interest in online communities and web3 onboarding, she has a passion for NFTs and the artists who create them. She is one of only a handful of web3 leaders to have received recognition from Salesforce, and is listed as one of its Web3 Advisory Board Members.

name: Usurping Binance Once And For All
description: For on chain volume to finally flip CEX volume we will need to win two intermeshed battles - order flow and liquidity. This talk focuses on the unique challenges that have plagued on-chain liquidity including the academic's favorite LVR. The talk will give an overview of all the proposed solutions to LVR across academia and industry as well as an update to which of these solutions are coming to market in 2024.

name: Designing Culture-Sensitive Hackathons for Empowering African Youth with Ethereum
description: Hackathons can potentially promote youth digital empowerment in Africa. But their design tends to follow the European and North American perspectives. Research has shown the key role of cultural aspects such as temporal awareness and temporal structure in fostering innovation during hackathons. Our project questions the status quo and seeks to investigate the approaches to designing culture-sensitive hackathons for empowering African youth within the Ethereum ecosystem. The results will contribute to the practical design of Ethereum hackathons and to the academic conversation around temporality and innovation.

name: From scarcity & speculation To utility & community
description: Web3 is distrupting music industry for the better. Hear about the experiences of how artists as they use digital platforms and create new ways to mix digital with physical experiences. See how Busker puts musicians and fans first, making real connections and giving real value to everyone involved. How musicians can use Web3 to fund their music projects and blend online and offline worlds. Come and find out about the future of music and community in the Web3 world.

name: Provable Compliance on Polygon Miden and beyond
description: Using Miden as an example, we expand on the advantages of building decentralised solutions utilising the potential of zk proofs and other technologies to substitute for centralised intermediaries traditionally acting as guardians and shielding users from market manipulation, excluding tainted funds and much more.

name: Scaling Communities, What Like It's Hard?
description:
My talk aims to challenge conventional concepts and give community leaders an unfiltered look behind the scenes: always-evolving strategies and operations. How one is building a community around a product, while building a product around a community. All in a scaled, automated way because the team won't be the one growing. 

Insights into some of our major challenges, gamified strategies, and what's coming next.

name: Wallet-2-wallet messaging must be secure, decentralized, private, and interoperable by design!
description:
Today's email and messenger services are either weakly encrypted or controlled by centralized authorities and lack the ability to work together across platforms. Web3 changes this with decentralized architectures and token- and key-based approaches that allow users to control their communications with their own keys.

However, web3-based messaging solutions are often still closed systems, have scalability issues, or use centralized components. As such, they are limited as interoperability protocols. 
To establish a connected and interoperable messaging ecosystem, a lean core messaging protocol is needed that is secure, private, and scalable by design, that can be used as a core messaging layer, and that can integrate other protocols or services without compromising privacy or security. The aim of the dm3 protocol is not to replace, but to connect all the good solutions that exist and to establish this core layer as public good.

name: Reputation for your projects: disco, otters, oranges, hats, and passports
description: Reputation is a core primitive for participation in DAOs and assigning different types of privileges and responsibilities to participants in Web3. But reputation is complex and difficult to parse. What are the approaches available today? Is offchain or onchain reputation better? What is a verifiable credential and how is it different from a Non-Transferable Token (NTT)? In this workshop we go through some of the tools, products, and approaches, and how different approaches work for different projects. Together, we'll explore your projects and how you can approach reputation either using existing tools or with your own reputation engines.

name: Exploring the Future of Account Abstraction in Ethereum
description:
Account abstraction (AA) represents a pivotal innovation in the Ethereum ecosystem, aiming to enhance flexibility, security, and user experience without compromising decentralization. This talk will provide a comprehensive overview of the journey from the initial proposal by Vitalik Buterin to the current implementation and future developments.

We will begin by revisiting the origins of ERC-4337, highlighting the key milestones and the evolution of the ERC-4337 standard. The presentation will delve into the significant challenges faced, particularly in ensuring censorship resistance and mitigating DoS vectors, and how these were addressed through strategic design choices.

Current progress will be examined, including the widespread adoption of ERC-4337 across major EVM networks and the ecosystem's rapid growth. Insights gathered from user operations will be discussed.

Looking forward, we will outline the modular roadmap for native AA, focusing on the Rollup Improvement Proposals (RIPs) designed to facilitate seamless adoption across Layer 2 (L2) chains. We will also explore the implications for Layer 1 (L1) and the steps needed to enshrine AA at the protocol level.

Finally, the talk will address the demand for enhanced capabilities in Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs) and the strategic approach to integrating these features without accruing technical debt. Attendees will gain a deeper understanding of the future direction of account abstraction and its critical role in advancing the Ethereum network.

Join us to explore the intricate roadmap of account abstraction, understand the ongoing developments, and engage in shaping the future of Ethereum's account model.

name: Join the Ethereum Protocol Fellowship
description:
At the heart of the Ethereum ecosystem lies core development, the work on the research and code that powers the Ethereum network, which includes client implementations, specifications, and other foundational aspects.

Come to learn about protocol development and the fellowship program which is accepting applications right now. If you want to dive into Ethereum consensus or execution, testing, scalability challenges and help to fill boxes of the Ethereum roadmap, this is a talk for you.

name: Liquid staking for DAOs: fixing a broken system
description:
This talk addresses the challenges faced by Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) in aligning incentives between token holders and governance participants. The current design of governance tokens, which combine financial and organizational utility, has led to misaligned incentives and inefficiencies. We will explore an innovative approach to solving these issues with Liquid Staking Tokens by separating the financial and governance utilities of tokens, enabling token holders to participate in DAOs based on their interests while maintaining the overall health and security of the organization.
The discussion will cover the benefits of this approach for both token holders and DAOs, including fostering active communities, protecting against governance attacks, and ensuring the long-term success of decentralized governance models. The talk will also analyze real-world case studies, such as the ENS DAO's recent implementation of a veto mechanism to address the risk of governance attacks arising from the disparity between the value of the DAO's treasury and the tokens represented by delegated voting power.
Furthermore, the potential implications of this approach for other prominent DAOs, such as Uniswap, will be examined.
This talk aims to provide valuable insights into how innovative approaches to aligning incentives can empower DAOs to navigate the challenges of decentralized governance and unlock the full potential of their communities.

name: Highly Available Ethereum Nodes with N-version design
description: As with all software, Ethereum nodes are exposed to faults in their underlying execution stack. Unstable execution environments can disrupt the availability of blockchain nodes' interfaces, resulting in downtime, and losses for service providers and users. This talk introduces the concept of N-Version nodes. This type of configuration relies on simultaneous execution of different Ethereum clients, in the line of Avizienis' N-Version programming vision.

name: Cairo - Writing Provable Programs
description: This talk explores Cairo, a unique language for writing programs on the blockchain. Unlike traditional code, Cairo programs are efficiently verifyable, guaranteeing their correctness without re-execution. Built with efficiency and security in mind, and inspired by Rust, Cairo enables developers to create secure and scalable smart contracts for Starknet, a layer 2 solution for Ethereum. In this talk we'll survey the current and future capabilities and features of Cairo.

name: VR as tool for design and research
description:
--what is VR (I always start with a funny picture of a ‘VR headset’); used tools/hardware/software
--role/application in design educations (Computational Design studio: designing with VR = application of VR in education, design studios)
--development in research (eg City at eye-level (tracking + eye-tracking), Urban Design for Improving Health (using VR for participation), Bio-Mirror (biometrics)) 
--application/integration in graduation projects (Sensing Urban Stress = Integration of all above in one project)
--future of VR? (as discussion: where is it heading, how to scale up in education, expectations for practice)

name: New climate narratives: Decentralisation and empowerment in the energy transition
description: Today, the climate crisis is the biggest threat to the continued survival of humanity. Climate scientists and energy-transition experts face the challenge of communicating the urgency of the situation in a way that brings as many people as possible on board as part of the solution without falling into doom and gloom narratives that can cause audiences to disconnect and lose hope. This talk will provide a short introduction into the current state of the climate crisis and share the (social) innovations and technological breakthroughs in the energy transition that show that effective action is not just possible and effective, but can also empower people and bring them together. If you're in the mood for some exciting climate and energy facts, and are looking for an optimistic perspective, this is the talk for you!

name: Time for Native Account Abstraction on L2s
description: What's wrong with using EOAs? When will quantum computers break ECDSA? Why should L2 be the first ones to solve Account Abstraction?

name: Blockchain for good - towards a more sustainable world
description: Advance sustainability through forest conservation with integrity, transparency and governance. Monthly satellite imaging and audit, involvement of academia for establishing cutting edge technology, and only backward looking tokenisation of actual effective carbon emission savings. Preventing greenwashing and establishing trust. Projects in Brasil already offset the F1 grandprix in Sao Paulo and more.

name: Creating Transformational Impact with Strategic Design and Futures Foresight: Tools and Techniques
description:
Embark on a journey with Ellery Studio as we explore the transformative power of participation, co-creation, and co-learning in shaping a real-life solarpunk future. In a world facing significant societal challenges, we'll examine how contemporary design methods can help guide us to better tomorrows.

Together, we'll investigate the often neglected human side of the adoption of renewable energy systems, shedding light on the intricate complexities of societal change. Fears, entrenched beliefs and sensitivities can be major obstacles for systemic progress or experimentation with new technologies. Embracing inclusivity and collaboration, we advocate for engaging citizens in a holistic manner, allowing diverse viewpoints to shape resilient and fair communities.

Furthermore, we'll take a closer look at the evolution of citizen participation, emphasizing the shift towards more inclusive and collaborative approaches in political practice, and highlighting the importance of diverse stakeholder engagement. Through real-world examples from Germany's energy transition landscape, we'll showcase how collective efforts can spark systemic shifts.

Goodie alert! As an added bonus, enjoy a collection of free playful infographic ebooks and science comics, offering low-threshold insights into diverse topics like the energy transition, sustainable transport, or cyber security.

name: Rjukan Solarpunk initiative
description:
Spreading organically through social media around the world, the term ‘solarpunk’ is a modality of dreaming real-life constructive change. Googling ‘solarpunk’ yields a complex interdisciplinary heritage that meshes literature, art and ecocritical traditions with contemporary technological innovation in the energy sector and urban planning fields. Not yet institutionalized and somewhat anarchist, Solarpunk sensibilities, knowledge, and attitudes can serve as the lodestar for art and culture built around the realities of climate emergency. Solarpunk can be imagined as a sustainable network structure of ideas, sensibilities and values, fully utilizing the potential of the internet to create new modes of human contact and communication. 

   Working with Solarpunk since 2019, we have however experienced a problem with the term. Due to the contemporary dominance of marketing logic within global aesthetics and visual culture, the style of Solarpunk have in many ways been dominated by what we know as greenwashing. We do however believe that the world really need a critical, authentic and vital Solarpunk - counterculture, and will therefore, in our interpretation of - and sharing through - the Solarpunk term use the IPCC SSP1-5 scenarios as the fundamental points of departure and essential core of interdisciplinary exchange of perspectives. https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGI_SPM.pdf https://ourworldindata.org/explorers/ipcc-scenarios https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_Socioeconomic_Pathways As more and more of institutional structures are turning ``green`` there is a need to clarify nuance within various green approaches. Obviously- the topic we are focusing on here is a rapidly moving target,living an active life in public discourse, and we can imagine ideas which today is considered utopian -like new economic narratives challenging the status qou, to be part of normalized discourse around the next corner.

  By maintaining a focus on the IPCC SSP scenarios, we can through the arts contribute to the ``backcasting from SSP 1 (the scenario called ``Sustainability``) and the artists involved with RSA will be able to contribute to public discourse with pragmatically useful perspectives, for which visual arts is actually perhaps the best suited discipline to enter into such a challenging territory as imagined futures in uncertain times.

name: Rewilding – nature conservation's punk?
description: Up until now, the world has failed to meet a single target to stop nature destruction. It's high time we reconsider our approach to nature conservation. A revolutionary concept gaining traction in Europe is Rewilding. It aims to restore natural processes, foster a nature-based economy, and reintegrate our own species with the natural world from which we've become strangely disconnected. Could Rewilding be to nature conservation what Solarpunk is to the Energy Transition and Permaculture is to agriculture? The grassroots organization "Collettivo Rewild Sicily" has set out to ground-truth rewilding principles in the heart of the Mediterranean –  initiatives focus on preventing wildfires (Anti-wildfire summer camp), practicing agroforestry (Seven Heavens forest), implementing regenerative grazing, and harnessing local ecological knowledge (CyberTracker) for a wilder, greener, and happier Sicily.

name: Closing Ceremony and Hackathon Result Announcements
Global finance is arriving on the blockchain: can we win the world, and keep our soul?
description:
The Real World Asset (RWA) trend in the Ethereum ecosystem has finally triggered the fusion of Ethereum's technology and the global financial system: tokenization is winning, and the EVM is everywhere.

But so are KYC, AML, CTF, securities lawyers, regulated custodians and the entire landscape of financial regulation. By the time they're done with us, will Ethereum be "just a database"? Will the cultural DNA of the system we built together be diluted too much by the next wave of change. How do we fight back against the risk of winning the world, but losing our souls in the process?

Vinay Gupta worked for the Ethereum Foundation 2014-2015. He project managed the launch of Ethereum. He is a director of Mattereum.de

name: How Ethereum can solve L2 Liquidity Fragmentation
description:
Ethereum is executing on its scaling roadmap with hundreds of L2's now planned or in production. The question on everyone's mind is - how do we combine these L2's to make them act like one chain with unified liquidity and shared sequencing.  
  
While shared sequencing has been fairly well covered, unified liquidity has not. This presentation will cover how all the major L2's are thinking about this problem and the solutions they're working on.

name: Advancing Towards ZK Fraud Proof - zkGo: Compiling L2 Geth into ZK-Compatible Wasm
description: Optimistic rollup suffers from the long settlement delay because of the multi-round interactive dispute game.  To accelerate the dispute game, ZK fault proof was recently proposed to challenge a malicious sequencer in a single transaction, significantly reducing gas costs and time compared to traditional fraud proofs.  To generate a ZK fault proof, the L2 Geth (a.k.a., op-program-client in Optimism)  needs to be emulated in an instruction set architecture (ISA), and then the execution result of the L2 Geth is proven by a zkVM. We choose WebAssembly (Wasm) - a widely adopted open-standard ISA and prove the execution of Wasm code using zkWasm, the state-of-the-art zkVM for Wasm developed by Delphinus Lab.  However, there are two main challenges in this path: 1, We cannot directly compile L2 Geth to Wasm with Go due to compilation errors.  To solve this problem, inspired by Arbitrum, we make minimum modifications to op-program-client to support Wasm compilation.  2, The compiled Wasm code by Go includes unclean exit code, floating-point instructions, and calls on ill-compatible host functions, which are unfriendly to ZK with high adaption cost.  To address this issue, we introduced zkGo - a customized Go compiler to produce Wasm code compatible with ZK prover.  As a result of these modifications, the execution of the compiled L2 Geth Wasm code can now be proven using zkWasm.

name: 10 years as a university crypto teacher
description:
What does it take to introduce a course on crypto at a university in 2014 when there are no such courses globally.
Challenges and benefits that make teaching crypto different from teaching other subjects.
How to give skills to students that help them build a carrier in crypto.
What have I learnt over the years.
How to build the first university course at Binance Academy.

name: The Future of Rollups - Interoperable, Performant and Sovereign
description:
In this talk, we dive into the world of L2s and the crucial role of sequencers. We will discuss various types of sequencers and explore how L2s can benefit from integrating with Espresso’s Shared Sequencer Marketplace. This marketplace allows L2s to auction off their block space to shared proposers including Ethereum mainnet proposers.  By attending, you will gain a deeper understanding of how Espresso's marketplace preserves the sovereignty for rollups’ sequencing rights, and enables the potential for new revenue streams such as capturing value for cross-chain MEV they create.

As the number of L2 and L3 chains increases, cross-chain interoperability becomes crucial. Join us to discover how Espresso’s sequencing marketplace will enable Ethereum L2s to seamlessly coordinate as sovereign chains.

name: Sequencers in Layer 2 Scaling Solutions and Beyond
description: In “Sequencers in Layer 2 Scaling Solutions and Beyond”, we will explore the key role of sequencers in L2 solutions, where they are responsible for ordering and executing transactions. I will highlight the prevalence of centralized sequencers in current L2 solutions, their benefits in terms of performance, but also the concerns related to centralization, security, and potential censorship. Then I will delve into decentralized sequencers, which utilize a decentralized network of nodes to perform sequencing, aiming to address the issues associated with centralization. Additionally, I will cover the emergence of shared sequencers, which allow multiple rollups to share a single decentralized network of sequencers, providing interoperability advantages between rollups.

name: Negatively Priced Blockspace
description:
Like oil in 2020, most blockspace is negatively priced. 

Besides Bitcoin and Ethereum's blockspace, blockspace is negatively priced. The actual utility of these chains are generating profit only for Bitcoin and Ethereum validators without subsidy. The native tokens of these chains are at least mostly decoupled from their chains' utility, which obscures their negatively priced blockspace. I'll show you how and why this is, and why it's not necessarily a bad thing! It might even be necessary.

name: The Future of zk-VM: Pioneering Optimization Techniques and Challenges
description:
1. Understanding zk-VM Architecture: Deep dive into the architecture of Valida zk-VM, highlighting design principles and why certain decisions are pivotal for optimization.
2. Identifying and Overcoming Bottlenecks: Analysis of common bottlenecks in zk-VMs, including computational challenges, memory constraints, and scalability issues. Share insights into how these bottlenecks were identified and strategies employed to mitigate them.
3. Advanced Optimization Techniques: Presentation of specific techniques and methodologies used to optimize zk-VMs. This covers algorithmic improvements, efficient coding practices, parallel processing, and more.
4. Case Studies or Examples: Real-world applications or theoretical models that illustrate the impact of optimization on zk-VM performance. These examples can help bridge theory with practice, offering tangible insights.
5. Future Directions and Innovations: Exploration of emerging trends, potential advancements in zk-VM technology, and how these developments could shape the future of privacy-preserving computations and blockchain technologies.
6. Practical Implications and Applications: Discussion on the broader impact of optimized zk-VMs on industries such as finance, healthcare, and beyond. Highlight how these advancements contribute to secure, efficient, and scalable solutions.
7. Community and Collaboration: Encouragement for continued research, development, and collaboration within the community to address unresolved challenges and unlock new possibilities in zk-VM technology.

name: How To DAO - how to build sustainable business
description:
DAOs were originally created to combine resources towards a common goal. This is still true today, but there are now many ways to achieve it. Through trial and error, we have developed various concepts of DAOs that are powerful tools for builders to coordinate and create value.

In this talk, we will examine some early experiments along with their outcomes and provide a guide on how to create a DAO for your next project. The focus will be on starting businesses that create value for everyone involved.

name: Understanding the importance of visibility and clarity on Ethereum's scaling solutions, driven by data and visualization.
description:
Growing Ethereum's ecosystem does not only require new rollups or projects deployed day-by-day, but also users that know what to use, where and what suits their needs best. Currently, this is complex and it's hard for new users, especially the ones that don't have the necessary technical background or have not been in crypto before. 

For real-world impact of Ethereum's ecosystem, it needs to grow also outside its current core users. Other techniques and ways to gather their interest and understanding have to be introduced.

One way to do this is to present data and visualizations in a easy-to-understand manner, and making it accessible by looking at people's behaviors, outside of crypto. 

We will explore how this can be done together, especially looking from the perspective of current and new developers in the space, educators, and investors that allow funding of new projects, also through novel mechanisms in the space.

name: Advancing Parallel EVM: Parallel I/O via Programmable Access List and Intelligent I/O Preloading
description:
In this talk, we delve into two innovative strategies to maximize the advantages of parallel I/O:
- EIP-7650: Programmable Access Lists - This mechanism empowers smart contract developers to proactively define access lists within their code. By facilitating parallel preloading of data, it significantly reduces transaction latency and optimizes gas costs.
- Intelligent I/O Preloading - This strategy optimizes contract execution by preloading commonly accessed data patterns. By doing so, it improves Ethereum's operational efficiency and transaction throughput.

Adoption of these parallel I/O strategies sheds light on higher transaction throughput and reduced operational costs, marking a step forward in the blockchain's evolution toward scalability.

name: Fullstack DApp Security: Going Beyond Smart Contract Audits
description: Starting from a smart contract audit, we'll look at what else can be done to improve the end-to-end security of our project, covering both tooling and development practices, all in the service of "shifting left" on security.

name: The Imperative of Security in dApps: Protecting the Decentralized Ecosystem
description: This talk will delve into the critical need for robust security in decentralized applications (dApps). It will cover the unique security challenges faced by dApps, including front-end security, backend security, wallets, e.t.c. The session will highlight real-world incidents of security breaches in the Dapp space, demonstrating the potential risks and consequences of inadequate security measures. Furthermore, it will outline the essential principles and strategies for developing secure dApps, emphasizing the importance of a proactive and comprehensive approach to security in the decentralized landscape.

name: Solidity Debugging meets Formal Methods
description:
**Problem**
At Runtime Verification our engineers and auditors noticed a lack of advanced Solidity debuggers, especially ones that combine the intuitiveness of classical interactive breakpoint-style debugging with the depth of symbolic execution.

**Solution**
To close this gap, we propose Simbolik: "the Symbolic Execution Solidity Debugger", a tool specifically designed to significantly lower the entry barrier for one of Computer Science's most advanced quality assurance techniques.

**What to expect**
While we want to elevate our audience’s knowledge, we don’t expect any prior knowledge of formal methods or symbolic execution. We've opted into an intuitive user interface that merges seamlessly into VSCode, empowering developers to start with classical debugging and progressively advance into expert bug-finding capabilities based on symbolic execution.

**How the audience benefits**
As you'd anticipate, our debugger offers all conventional functionalities, from setting breakpoints to stepping through code (both at the Solidity and EVM levels), inspecting variables, and navigating call stacks. Its symbolic capabilities set our tool apart: it can begin debugging with arbitrary symbolic storage and call data, allowing users to explore the comprehensive branching control flow graph and delve into the conditions assigned to each path. Essentially, debug a function once, and you've probed every potential behavior it could manifest.

**What we show**
In our session, we will exemplify the debugger's core functionalities. Together, we'll uncover how it excels in detecting nuanced bugs, which often elude more traditional methodologies like testing, fuzzing, concrete debugging, and static analysis.

name: Secure Reactive Web3 for Everyone
description:
Building Web3 applications that require fast and secure on-chain interactions between users is notoriously hard due to the data latency of a blockchain infrastructure and the difficulty of securely accessing on-chain data from a Web UI in general. In this presentation, we discuss how to make secure reactive Web3 a reality using the concept of microchains developed by the Linera protocol.

In Linera, wallets—mobile or in the browser—track the full application state of their users and execute data queries locally. The protocol is designed to optimize latency from transaction creation to on-chain finalization, all the way to the notification of connected user wallets. Linera uses Wasm and Web2 standards such as GraphQL to offer developers a familiar environment and greater compatibility with traditional platforms.

name: Pitfalls of building public goods with permissionless work
description: OnlyDust is pioneering a new model of sustainable open source public goods development – contributors get paid for every merged PR. I'll share what I learned leading the development of Konoha (https://github.com/CarmineOptions/governance) , a public good toolkit for DAOs on Starknet that will need functionality such as governance, treasury management and vote token staking.

name: Death Economics: Why Crypto Can't Solve Social Problems
description: If you think you're designing a crypto that will solve social and ecological problems, think again. Your crypto won't solve the problem you wish it would. This is because the destruction of the planet and erosion of culture are only "side effects" of the economy because we put the word "side" before the word "effect". We are brainwashed to believe that the "invisible hand" in a death economy will provide a fair market value for things, despite all evidence to the contrary. Don't believe the death cult. Cure the mind virus in this quick talk that will help you redesign currency in a way that is aligned with creating real value in the world.

name: Building the first Real-Time Blockchain, and what you can do with it
description: MegaETH is real-time Ethereum. It provides a developer and user experience more akin to a modern computer while retaining every benefit and familiarity of Ethereum. MegaETH is enabled by two key techniques: node specialization, which concentrates the heavy lifting work to just a few nodes, and a hyper-optimized EVM execution environment that pushes throughput, latency, and resource efficiency closer to the hardware limit.

name: Forensics in Web3: How and When
description:
In Q1 2024, we've seen a positive trend: a significant portion of stolen funds has been successfully recovered or frozen. This success underscores the importance of adhering to protocol-specific recovery steps and conducting thorough forensic analyses to identify and neutralize attackers.
In the aftermath of a blockchain breach, navigating the road to recovery requires following tailored protocols specific to the affected blockchain. Similarly, tracing and exposing hackers through forensic investigations demands a nuanced approach, varying across different networks.
During this session, we'll discuss practical strategies for incident recovery, emphasizing the need for tailored approaches depending on the blockchain involved. Additionally, we'll explore the complexities of forensic analysis and hacker identification, shedding light on the unique challenges presented by different network architectures.

name: Non Fungible Brain: A Web3 Approach to Democratizing Funding and Research for Alzheimer's Disease and Empowering Caregivers
description: Non Fungible Brain merges art, science, and blockchain technology to create unique digital collectibles (NFTs) that raise awareness and funding for Alzheimer's disease research. The project explores the decentralized nature of both the human brain and blockchain, aiming to foster collaboration among scientists, artists, patients, and the blockchain community. By potentially incorporating web3 mechanisms like Quadratic Funding, Non Fungible Brain could further democratize funding allocation and empower the community to directly contribute to the fight against Alzheimer's.

name: Beyond Coverage: Mutation Testing
description: Code coverage has a long history of being used as the metric for evaluating the quality of tests, but it's not always an appropriate metric. Mutation testing, by running tests against modified code, can do a better job at identifying faults. How can smart contract developers leverage the power of mutation to improve their tests? What tools can they use to automate this process?

name: Zero Knowledge privacy in action
description:
Remember the prompts you get when you enter a restricted website, confirming whether you're at least 18 years old? Why is it ok for anyone just to click "Yes" with zero proofs?

I claim it's ok because there haven't been tools to easily (and securely) verify the age. Zero Knowledge technology provide this possibility.

I'll walk through the steps needed for this kind of project and showcase a small, concrete project I built for this.

name: The Paranoid Developer’s Guide to Safer Smart Contracts
description:
At the heart of our presentation is the philosophy that "trust is a luxury." This mantra isn't about skepticism for its own sake but a call to arms for developers to adopt a mindset where verification and testing become second nature. The goal is to inspire developers to not only adopt stronger security habits but to fundamentally rethink how they approach the development and deployment of smart contracts.

We will delve into a suite of sophisticated techniques that we employ daily to safeguard our projects. From unit testing, to fuzz testing and formal verification. We will go beyond traditional methods and introduce participants to advanced strategies such as on-chain invariance monitoring and the strategic use of circuit breakers. These tools are not just safety nets but essential components of a proactive security strategy, designed to catch issues before they become disasters.

But this talk is more than just a quick rundown of tools and techniques. It's a call to embrace a culture of security that permeates every stage of the development process. By sharing our unique approaches and the lessons we've learned, we aim to equip other developers with not just the tools but also the mindset needed to elevate the security of their projects.

name: Escape Hatches: Urgent Anti-Censorship Solutions for Specific Transactions
description: We aim to bring self-custody to billions, but the decentralization of sequencers may initially be imperfect and delayed. Proven tools like escape hatches in StarkEx have been crucial, successfully serving thousands in platforms like Sorare and dYdX. Implementing these in a permissionless blockchain like Starknet, where anyone can build censorship-resistant apps, is key to reaching millions. It’s essential for developers to recognize this as a viable way to provide self-custody to a massive audience.

name: Introducing web3:// - Decentralized Access Protocol for EVM
description: As the Ethereum scalability initiatives, including data availability (DA) and Layer 2 (L2) solutions, progress, they pave the way for massive adopted fully on-chain applications. Yet, an essential component remains absent in Ethereum's evolution: a decentralized protocol facilitating direct access to on-chain resources like NFT images and on-chain websites. In this talk, we introduce the ERC-4804/6860: Web3 URL Standard. This standard defines HTTP-style web3:// links to navigate to on-chain resources maintained by smart contracts. As a result, it effectively transforms the Ethereum virtual machine (EVM) into an unstoppable decentralized HTTP server. We'll delve into the various methods for accessing these resources through web3://, including gateways, command-line interfaces (CLI), browser extensions, and browsers with native support. Additionally, we'll showcase several groundbreaking fully on-chain applications that leverage web3://, such as Vitalik's blog, dynamic NFTs, and a completely on-chain blogging platform.

Pre-confirmation is a mechanism that provides users with a fast guarantee that their transaction will be included in the next block, improving user experience and potentially increasing profit for activities like arbitrage.

The researcher explains the roles of two main actors in this system: bidders, who are willing to pay for pre-confirmations, and pre-confirmation providers, who can credibly promise transaction inclusion. Primav has developed MavCommit as an open network where anyone can participate as either role.

Primav's solution includes a side chain with fast block times for settlement and a decay mechanism incentivizing timely pre-confirmations. The protocol also emphasizes privacy for bids and commitments through encryption and special cryptographic commitments.

description: Clip
aiDescription:
The video outlines the concept of execution tickets and their role in managing MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) within blockchain protocols. The speaker discusses ongoing research focused on capturing MEV at the protocol level through execution tickets, which were first proposed to separate the consensus chain (beacon chain) from the execution chain. They explain how this separation allows for randomization to prevent issues like multi-block MEV and liveness problems.

The talk delves into data analysis on multi-block MEV, examining whether there's value in controlling multiple slots consecutively. Preliminary findings suggest more multi-slot sequences occur than expected by chance, but the reasons behind this are not fully understood.

The speaker also covers simulation results of different mechanism designs for selling execution tickets, such as auctions and pricing mechanisms. Initial takeaways indicate challenges in achieving decentralization and transferring existing pricing models like EIP-1559 directly to execution tickets.

Future steps include making simulation agents more sophisticated with strategic bidding and updating the multi-block MEV data analysis with newer information. The talk concludes with a Q&A session clarifying how execution tickets can redistribute MEV earnings from validators to all token holders, potentially benefiting a broader set of stakeholders within the ecosystem.

name: Defending malicious behavior in federated learning with blockchain
description: Clip

The video features Jiahao Sun, the founder and CEO of Flock, discussing the company's mission and technology. Flock is a pun for federative learning blockchain, an idea stemming from a paper published in NeurIPS 2022 and further detailed in the journal "Transitioning AI." Jiahao's background includes working in traditional finance as head of AI at Eurobank Canada and as a researcher at Imperial College London.

Flock aims to solve data silo issues in industries like finance and healthcare by combining federated learning with blockchain technology. Federated learning occurs on devices like smartphones, where data stays local while only model weight changes are sent to improve collective models. However, there's a risk of centralized control and data misuse, which Flock addresses using blockchain for transparency and security.

The platform introduces an incentive mechanism where good behaviors are rewarded, and bad actors are penalized, ensuring honest participation. The system uses random selection for proposers who contribute to model training and voters who validate results. Malicious attempts are thwarted through this process, maintaining high accuracy even with a significant presence of bad actors.

Jiahao also discusses experiments with the Kaggle Learning Club dataset that demonstrate the effectiveness of Flock's approach compared to traditional federated learning under malicious conditions.

name: Swarm: Future storage Now! || Niki Papadatou
description:
What is Swarm? An open source web3 project, a decentralised and distributed network for data storage, ready to power the next generation with censorship-resistant, unstoppable, serverless dapps.
An exciting year has passed that has brought Swarm to the next page with even more secure data, on a stronger network, and even more exciting features to come!
aiDescription:
This video features Nikki, the product owner of a core development team, discussing the decentralized data storage solution called Swarm. She explains that Swarm is an open-source project within the Ethereum ecosystem, utilizing Gnosis chain smart contracts and powered by a specific token for economic sustainability. Users can store private and secure files, operate nodes, or build decentralized apps on Swarm.

Nikki details the network's structure, including its peer-to-peer protocol with libp2p library, data storage and retrieval systems, and application layers for development. She describes how nodes operate in neighborhoods to ensure redundancy and what happens when a node's storage capacity is exceeded.

The presentation covers how files are stored in chunks across the network and retrieved using hashes. It also highlights incentive mechanisms for storage and bandwidth contributions to the network.

Looking back at the previous year, Nikki shares advancements such as Erasure Codes for data security, improvements in storage incentives to prevent cheating, adjustments in token supply through community governance, and increased community engagement with new proposals for features being discussed transparently.

Future updates include Access Control Trees for more secure file permissions, Neighborhood Hopping for better reward chances, improved staking mechanisms allowing movement of increased value stakes to other nodes, optimized node resources for better rewards management, multi-chain support to pay with native tokens

name: Swarm's Unstoppable Features || Noah Maizels
description: In this presentation we explore the underlying technical design choices which enable Swarm's unstoppable and censorship-resistant characteristics. We will take a deep dive into the technical features powering Swarm, such as its chunk-based storage model, which distributes file segments across a network to prevent data loss and censorship. We'll also discuss the Swarm's approach to storage incentives, and content addressing. Additionally, we will learn how optional features like encryption and erasure coding further enhance privacy and data persistence.
aiDescription:
In this video, Noah, a member of the DevRel team with a focus on documentation and educational articles, explains the features that make Swarm an unstoppable platform. He breaks down complex concepts into plain language for a broad audience. The presentation covers three main characteristics of Swarm: data persistence, data availability, and censorship resistance.

Noah delves into Swarm's chunk-based storage model, where files are split into chunks and distributed across the network to ensure redundancy and resistance to network changes. He also discusses the anonymity of upload and download requests for privacy.

The incentives model is explored, detailing how storage nodes are rewarded for honesty through a game-like mechanism that penalizes censorship and ensures data integrity.

Payment and addressing models are explained, highlighting how anyone can contribute to keeping data online through postage batches and how content addressing ensures consistent references for files.

Lastly, Noah touches on optional features like encryption for privacy and erasure coding for data protection against loss or large-scale network failures.

The video concludes with a demo using VJS, demonstrating how to create postage batches, upload data, and download it with encryption and erasure coding enabled. Noah encourages viewers to try out these features themselves.

name: Panel: Optimizing Node Operations in Swarm: Economic and Technical Insights

aiDescription:
The video features a speaker named Cserteh Linn who introduces a panel discussion with Yuriy Barabak and Kalom, focusing on topics relevant to node operators within a decentralized storage network. The agenda includes an overview of the node operators' role in the ecosystem and a discussion on upcoming changes that could impact their operations. They explain how storage providers, who are full nodes with staking capabilities, offer storage space to data providers in exchange for payment. Data users also pay for bandwidth when downloading data. While there is an indirect connection between data providers and users outside of the Swarm network, node operators have costs such as running hardware, bandwidth, electricity, personnel, and staking.

The panel addresses recent updates that affect node operators' profitability by discussing the concept of "freezing" nodes in the storage incentives lottery. Freezing occurs when a node's cryptographic hash doesn't match the chosen "oracle of truth," leading to temporary exclusion from the game. To mitigate harsh penalties for honest nodes due to imperfect system syncing, they've implemented "stochastic freezing," which only gives a 20% chance of being frozen if a mismatch occurs.

The discussion includes technical details about the probability of freezing before and after updates, noting improvements from 30% down to below 5%. This
